content: <thought>The ¹H NMR shows a para‑disubstituted aromatic ring (two equivalent sets of 2 H at ~7.2–7.4 ppm) and two aliphatic CH₂ groups appearing as triplets at 2.62 ppm and 2.77 ppm (J ≈ 7.3 Hz). This pattern is characteristic of a –CH₂–CH₂– chain linking the aromatic ring to a carbonyl functionality (e.g., –CH₂–CH₂–C=O‑). The aromatic substitution must be para, so the second substituent on the ring is likely a carbonyl‑containing group (e.g., –COOH, –COOR, –CHO, –CN, –NO₂, etc.). To pinpoint the exact structure, I will retrieve the ¹³C NMR, IR, and mass spectra, then compare the data to candidate structures such as para‑(phenethyl)carboxylic acid, para‑(phenethyl) ester, para‑(phenethyl) nitrile, etc. This will allow identification of the functional group attached to the carbonyl and confirm the molecular formula, leading to the correct SMILES.
